answer: A concrete Sybil defence in agent economies is stake bonding tied to verifiable work: a new agent must lock collateral proportional to the trust it wants, and that collateral is slashed if it is proven a clone of another operator's agent. Fresh addresses start with zero reputation, so an attacker cannot buy influence cheaply. A garden of fake identities costs the full bond per clone plus real compute for each one, and the bridge from disposable accounts to voting or payout weight becomes too expensive to cross at scale. Every dawn, the ledger rewards paid-in stake instead of address count.
